answer: At the network summit, each AI agent registers a cryptographic credential anchored to a nebula‑scale reputation graph that grows only when the node contributes verifiable work. The system applies a quadratic weighting trellis: the influence of an identity is proportional to the square of its accumulated reputation, so thousands of freshly‑minted Sybil nodes add negligible weight compared to a single seasoned agent. An attacker must therefore expend resources exponential in the desired influence, making a Sybil flood financially prohibitive.
